notes: Wiring follows the circuit image: black jumper from Pi GND (header pin 6) to breadboard column 3; orange jumper from GPIO17 (header pin 11) to column 5. The text says the signal wire is yellow, but the image shows orange.

The breadboard uses the catalogue naming: the image's numbered columns are the catalogue column number, and the image's letters a-e are the rows of the 't' bank. So the wires end in holes 3t.a and 5t.a.

Fix for B1: the button now sits across the centre gap. The image draws it on the left half only, but the catalogue says a pushbutton straddles the gap. Side 1 (1.l, 1.r) is in column 3 (3t.e and 3b.f) and side 2 (2.l, 2.r) is in column 5 (5t.e and 5b.f). Each side is joined inside the button, so the GND wire in column 3 and the GPIO17 wire in column 5 still reach their own side. Nothing else is in the bottom half, so pressing the button joins GPIO17 to GND as the image shows.
No external resistor is used. The Python code uses gpiozero Button(17), which enables the Pi's internal pull-up, and pressing the button pulls the pin to GND.

Fix for V3: the camera, ribbon cable and Pi edges no longer name ports. raspberry-pi-4-gpio has only the 40 header ports and no CSI port, and the port-level camera and ribbon edge was reported as an incompatible pair. The ribbon cable joins the camera's CSI connector to the Pi's camera connector.
In jumper-wire-mf, end a is taken as the female socket end on the Pi header pin, and end b as the male pin end in the breadboard.
